A steep alpine village climbs a switchback road in tight cobalt-shadowed zigzags, every terrace stacked above the last, flock snow thick on the burnt-orange tile roofs, grain-of-wheat bulbs burning amber in rows of windows, and on the topmost bend a wooden sled rests nose-first in a drift, pointed downhill, ready, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

A frozen canal cuts between mustard-yellow townhouses whose reflections shiver in the blue-black ice below; stone bridges arch across at three distances, each one smaller and hazier than the last; a skating pond blazes with warm lamplight at the far end, and one upstairs window stands open with its curtain pushed aside.

A pine forest crowds a cut sleigh road that curves hard left and disappears into absolute dark between the trunks; the pines are bottle-green to their tips, dusted white; a single brass lantern hangs from a branch mid-road, still swinging, and a second lantern is already around the bend and out of sight, its glow bleeding orange through the needles, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

A harbour freezes mid-tide, three cobalt-hulled fishing boats locked into the ice at tilt, their rigging furred white; a fourth boat has been hauled up onto the quay with its oars still shipped in the rowlocks, abandoned mid-haul; behind the quay, lit warehouse windows stack in crimson-curtained rows up the hill, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

A cliff monastery clings to a vertical sandstone face, its butter-yellow walls dissolving into cloud from halfway up; linked stairways cut into the rock climb level after level and vanish into grey mist; every arched window glows deep amber, and a washing line strung between two upper balconies holds small robes lifting in the updraft.

A mountain railway loops a snowbound peak, the scarlet engine mid-curve on a high viaduct, steam boiling sideways in the wind; the track sweeps into a tunnel mouth on the far side and the mountain has a whole unseen flank beyond; the viaduct's arches frame a valley floor five levels below, faintly blue in the distance.

A bakery street wakes at blue predawn, the sky above the rooftops a deep indigo bruise; every chimney breathes white, and the ground-floor windows of one long building glow furnace-gold from inside; a painted loaf on the shuttered door-panel marks the one shop whose lights have been burning all night, flour dust drifting at the transom.

A fir plantation spreads to the glass on all sides, the trees deep-shadow green and close; far inside, one timber cabin burns with warm buttercup light at every window, and a woodpile stacked against the east wall casts a long red-shadow stripe; a ladder leans against the cabin's roof peak, reaching toward a snow-loaded gutter.

A whole night city fills every plane to the far edge, a million lighted windows in amber and gold climbing towers, streets glowing orange-sodium in the canyons below; at the centre a roof garden blazes acid green under its own lights; a single water tower at the back of the scene wears a painted crescent moon on its belly.

A thunderstorm stands directly over one small farm in flat open country; the cloud is charcoal-purple from its anvil to the ground, lit from within by a travelling bolt caught mid-branch; the farmhouse below shines a raw brass-gold against the surrounding darkness, and an open barn door swings outward on its own momentum into the electric light.

A green aurora unreels over a tin-roof cabin on a treeless plain, the sky rolling from deep teal to acid green in broad bands; the cabin's single window throws a yellow rectangle onto blue snow; a rain gauge bolted to the cabin's south wall reads an impossible height because the cylinder is capped with a small dome of its own ice.

A summer meadow stretches to a far hedgerow, knee-deep in buttercup yellow and ox-blood poppy red, dandelion clocks and seed-pollen drifting through the warm air instead of flakes; a low stone wall crosses the middle distance and a wooden gate stands half-open in it, its shadow stretching long into the grass below.

A coral reef wall drops away from a shallow shelf, the colonies cobalt and deep plum in the filtered light, silt drifting in slow curtains instead of snow; a crevice halfway down glows from inside with bioluminescent teal, and a brain coral the size of a doorstep sits at the shelf edge, its grooves packed with pale gold polyps.

A volcano's flank drops to a black-sand beach village of flat-roofed houses in burnt orange and raw white; warm grey ash drifts down like snow; the fishing boats drawn up the beach have their nets draped over poles to dry, the nets furred now with pale ash; a second cinder cone rises behind the main peak, its own faint smoke joining the column, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

A carnival blazes on a flat field at night, the ferris wheel mid-rotation with every gondola lit gold-and-scarlet; strings of bulbs loop tent to tent in low catenary arcs; the wheel's reflection smears bright on a wet black path below, and at the far edge of the fairground the lights thin out into darkness and a road winds away.

A desert caravan crosses a dune crest at sundown, the sand a saturated burnt orange, camels in a line of receding silhouettes against a sky the colour of raw brass; fine sand drifts horizontally across the scene instead of falling snow; the lead camel carries a rolled carpet of deep plum across its hump, its fringe lifting in the grit-wind, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

A moon base clusters on a grey crater rim, silver domes linked by low corridors, slow grey dust lifting and falling in the weak gravity instead of flakes; one dome is larger and its porthole glows amber; a tractor-vehicle sits outside the airlock with its scoop arm raised mid-job, caught in the act, casting a long shadow toward the crater floor.

A jungle temple rises through canopy in acid-green and moss-grey stone, a stepped pyramid shedding a rain downpour; water sheeting off every tier catches the light; carved serpent balustrades line the main stair all the way to a doorway at the summit that glows deep amber from inside; vines thick as rope hold one stone block open from the wall.

A cherry orchard covers a hillside in full bloom, every tree throwing white-pink petals sideways on a wind instead of snow; between the rows a low stone irrigation channel runs with fast blue water; one tree at the crest leans at a dramatic angle, its root-plate lifting the soil, its blossoms shaking in a private gust from the exposed ridge.

An ocean liner ploughs open Atlantic at night, bow rising on a wave, spray coming over the rail in a white sheet; every porthole on three decks burns amber in a long horizontal streak; the stern tapers into darkness and the wake fans out luminous green-blue behind, the foam still swirling in the middle distance as if the ship just passed, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

A hot-air-balloon meet lifts from a green field at first light, four balloons already at different heights — one cobalt, one scarlet, one acid yellow, one deep plum — trailing their baskets below; the ground crew on the field are tiny by their scale, implying the height the lowest balloon has already reached; a fifth envelope still lies collapsed on the grass, breathing colour into itself, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

A crag castle stands on a vertical rock column above deep fog, its drawbridge extended and blazing with a line of torches in iron brackets; the portcullis is raised and the gate-passage beyond it glows orange; the castle has two curtain walls, one higher than the other, and the far tower behind them shows lit arrow-loops stacked up its full height.

A valley of long-necked dinosaurs spreads to a distance of forested ridges, the giants mid-stride between cycad stands in the warm ochre light of an ashfall; pale grey volcanic flakes drift down onto their backs and collect along their spines; a collapsed tree in the foreground reveals its root plate, red clay clinging, as if knocked only moments ago.

A rooftop city of chimneys crowds every level, Tudor-red brick stacks in clusters of three and five, some capped with spinning cowls, one broken and still; a whole grid of rooftops descends to a courtyard far below where a skylight burns bright teal; pigeons wheel in a loose spiral over the middle distance, their undersides lit gold by the chimneys' own warmth.

A cliff ice-shelf calves into black Arctic water at the far edge, a cathedral-blue mass mid-fall caught at the instant of separation, spray already fanning; behind the shelf the glacier continues back into a mountain bowl still in deep shadow; along the intact ice-wall, horizontal strata in ox-blood rust and mineral white record centuries in plain parallel lines.

An underground station platform stretches beneath barrel-vaulted tiles of cream and deep cobalt, the walls curving overhead in close mosaic arcs; iron pillars march the platform's length in ox-blood red, each capped with a disc lamp burning amber; the tunnel mouth at the far end pulses with a growing warm-gold smear of headlights, and a single bench at mid-platform holds a folded newspaper pressed flat by the rising tunnel dust.

A road tunnelled through a giant redwood drops into the trunk's dark interior, headlights pooling butter-yellow on the close bark walls and pushing mist ahead in soft rolling waves; the grove rises beyond the far opening in columns of acid-green shadow stacked against a pale sky; lichen mottles the bark in grey-gold patches and the road curves gently rightward inside the wood, the exit glowing small and bright, a gate of light.

A great dam wall carries its crest road in a long ox-blood arc above the gorge, the reservoir behind it a flat slate-cobalt mirror dissolving into mist at the far shore; spillways pour white water in thundering sheets down the curved face and the spray boils upward in drifting veils of silver; a signal lamp on the eastern pier burns deep amber, its light shivering in the wet air beside the roaring fall.

A raft rides mid-rapid in a red-rock canyon, the river acid-green and white between walls of burnt-orange sandstone that rise sheer to a slot of cobalt sky; a rope line strung between two boulders marks a sandbar camp downstream where an ox-blood tent glows with interior amber and a second tent stands open-flapped in the current air; spray drifts upstream in long pale threads; a paddle floats loose at the raft's stern, turning slowly in the eddy.

A terraced vineyard climbs above a river bend in tight ox-blood and amber rows, every vine stripped to its winter cane, the cut stems rust-dark against pale clay soil; the river below curves away into deep cobalt haze; a press house at the top row burns with one butter-yellow window, its door ajar and spilling warmth onto the highest terrace, and copper-brown leaves drift down the slope in slow turns.

A cable car climbs a steep city street through layered fog, its brass-yellow body mid-haul between trestles, the twin tracks shining slick cobalt below; mustard-yellow and deep plum townhouses stack the hill on both flanks, their upper windows dissolving into grey; bay water glimmers at the foot of the street, pewter and wide; mist drifts in slow rolls between the rooflines, and the cable car's forward door swings on its latch.

A ghost town main street drops to a dry creek bed between bone-pale timber frontages, their facades bleached and leaning, every window dark save one saloon pane burning amber deep inside; the street runs straight to a far mesa wall the colour of burnt orange; a tumbleweed rolls mid-street in a slow arc toward the lit window, and dust drifts in pale curtains across the plank boardwalks.

An oil platform stands in a storm sea, its four acid-green derrick legs braced wide in churning grey-black water; every deck burns white along its guardrail, level stacked above level, and the flare at the crown roars a deep ox-blood orange against a bruise-purple sky; a supply line trails taut off the leeward edge into the swell, and spray drifts in dense sheets across the lower decks.

A stone refuge hut sits on a high col between two cobalt-shadowed ridges, its granite walls the colour of pale ash, one window burning deep amber against a sky of plum and grey; a marked path of cairns descends both flanks, each cairn smaller and hazier toward the valley; snow drifts in slow diagonals across the col, and the hut's storm shutter hangs open on its hinge, catching the wind.

An ice hotel of carved translucent blocks shoulders into a treeline of bottle-green spruce, its walls lit from within to a deep aquamarine bruise shot through with veins of cobalt; a tall archway frames the entrance, its keystone block glowing butter-yellow where a lantern hangs just inside; carved corridors recede into blue interior distance, level after level of cool radiance; snow drifts through the arch in slow spirals; a single fur glove rests on the threshold step, unclaimed.

A container port spreads across its deep-water berth under a moonless acid-green and cobalt sky, gantry cranes arched in bright halogen rows above stacks of ox-blood and mustard-yellow boxes ranked to the far quay wall; a broad-hulled ship idles alongside, its superstructure blazing with white working lights tier on tier; the port road loops behind the stacks and disappears inland between warehouse flanks; snow drifts through the crane lights, and one gantry hook swings slow arcs above an open hatch.

An apple orchard drops to a cider-press barn at the low end of the field, the trees heavy and acid-green, crates of russet and butter-yellow fruit stacked four high along the near fence; the barn doorway burns warm amber at the centre of everything, the press wheel visible just inside the threshold; leaves spin and tumble down between the rows in long diagonal lines, and one crate at the top of a stack has tilted forward, half-tipped, mid-fall.

An undersea dome city rests on a cobalt-black seabed, its linked chambers glowing through silt-clouded water in rings of amber and pale ox-blood; curved corridors connect dome to dome, each junction lit at the join; a submersible noses into its docking collar on the lowest tier, running lights still burning green; one upper porthole pulses with a warmer, slower light, as though something is passing close inside.

A white stupa crowns a bare hilltop, its dome the cold clean white of fresh lime, its spire tipped in deep plum-red lacquer against a slate sky; prayer flags in mustard-yellow and cobalt stream outward from the crown on four long lines; a stone stair climbs the southern face in tight switchbacks, each landing edged with a small butter-lamp bowl; one flag has come loose at its knot and lifts free at the tip, riding the wind.

An acacia savanna opens at a red-clay waterhole where the flat-topped trees thin to amber grassland beyond; the lodge on the rise burns with ochre lamplight in every wide window, its deep veranda casting rust-shadow bars across the dust-pale terrace below; a track cuts from the waterhole through copper-dry scrub and climbs the ridge to lose itself over the far side, and a tin-roofed outbuilding beside the lodge holds one door kicked wide and swinging.

An airship rides its mooring mast above a night city spread cobalt and ox-blood to every edge of the world, its vast envelope a deep plum cigar against the ink sky; the gondola burns cream-warm at each porthole, and a gangway angles out from the forward hatch to the mast platform; snow drifts past the envelope in long diagonals, and the gangway door hangs wide, still moving on its hinge.

A gold-rush sluice camp straddles a mountain creek in a crook of spruce-dark valley, the long wooden sluice boxes running bank to bank on rough trestle legs, creek water foam-white in the channels; canvas tents glow mustard-yellow from lanterns inside, each one a warm oblong against the grey-blue snowfall; at the nearest tent a flap has been pushed half-open, its corner still lifted on the cold air.

A striped tulip field runs in flat bands of acid green, deep plum, and burnt orange all the way to a horizon of pale pewter sky; the bulb barn beside the straight canal road is bone-white with a broad ox-blood door rolled half-open on its runner; the road follows the canal dead-straight to where both vanish into the colour-banded distance, and a single petal drifts across the water's surface, still spinning.

A beaver lodge humps from the still centre of a dusk pond, its mud-and-stick dome dark against water that holds the last cobalt of the sky; the dam curves from bank to bank in a low pale arc, a thread of current spilling quiet over its lip; a cabin burns butter-yellow across the water, its reflection broken into wavering bars; moths drift and circle the cabin window, their wings catching the warm light.

A wind-turbine ridge stretches along the high spine of a hill at amber sunset, the blades turning slow against a sky the colour of burnt orange bleeding into deep plum at the zenith; a grey service road threads between the towers and drops over the far edge toward an unseen valley; chaff drifts in slow spirals through the warm air; one turbine stands feathered and motionless, its nacelle turned sideways to the wind, waiting.

A surf cove opens between two ox-blood sandstone headlands that crowd the water into a tight crescent of pale sand; a lifeguard tower stands on its stilts at the high-tide line, its acid-green railing salt-bleached to sage; a wave breaks full across the mouth of the cove, its face briefly translucent before it folds; beach fires burn in a scattered amber chain along the sand, spray drifting inland through their light, and one fire's driftwood log rolls a half-turn in the wash.

An old stone bridge lined with shops on both sides spans a slow pewter river in three broad arches, the shopfronts a pressed row of mustard-yellow and ox-blood plaster above the parapets; every upper window burns warm amber over the water, and the reflections ripple in long gold columns downstream; the far bank rises into a steep tangle of rooftops and gabled dormers; a painted shutter on the middle-span shop hangs on one hinge, snow settling on its sill.

A coastal highway cuts a raw ledge into a chalk-white cliff face, the road bending hard around a blunt headland, one car's amber beams sweeping the curve and lighting the stone wall ahead in a moving wedge of gold; the road climbs back inland on the far side and vanishes into dark; spray rises from the surf below in slow-rolling veils of pale grey; a safety chain across a lay-by hangs loose at one end, swaying.

A sunken galleon leans into a coral reef in water the colour of deep plum shading upward through cobalt to acid green near the surface, its hull split amidships and its masts raked at steep angles, fish threading the rigging in loose silver drifts; the stern lantern burns a steady amber through the current, casting long rippling light across the reef below; silt rises in thin pale columns from the disturbed sand, and the capstan is turning, very slowly, on its own.

A row of pastel beach huts stretches along a salt-bleached promenade, their tongue-and-groove faces painted mint, coral, and buttercup-yellow in strict alternation; a timber boardwalk runs the full length and curves out of frame at both ends; spray drifts across the lower planks in thin white veils; every hut stands shuttered save one, its ox-blood door flung wide, two striped deckchairs angled toward the sea, one still rocking.

A mountaineers' base camp spreads across a grey glacier moraine, the tents ox-blood and acid-green against the pale rubble, their guy-ropes frosted white; prayer flags run in long diagonal lines from a central pole, the colours faded to soft ochre and cobalt; above, the icefall pitches in broken seracs toward a summit ridge lost in grey cloud, and snow drives sideways across the upper slopes; one tent door hangs open, its flap lifting in the glacier wind.

A rope footbridge crosses a deep gorge whose walls drop through layers of ochre and plum sandstone into a river far below, the water a thin acid-green ribbon catching what light reaches it; mist drifts upward through the chasm in slow revolving columns; a lit hut burns amber on each rim, their windows facing each other across the drop; on the near side the hut's door stands half-open, its latch swinging.

A kayak rides a mangrove creek where arching roots rise from copper-dark water in interlocking vaults, their undersides pale and barnacled; the creek bends twice and opens at the mouth onto a lit jetty whose planks glow butter-yellow in the dusk; fireflies drift through the root canopy in slow loops, each one leaving a faint smear of gold among the deep-shadow green; the kayak's paddle rests across the gunwales, one blade still dripping.

A five-tiered pagoda rises beside a koi pond among maples whose canopy burns in layered ox-blood and amber; a stone humpback bridge arches over the pond's narrow waist, its reflection broken by slow-drifting leaves that turn in the current and pass beneath; a lit lantern hangs from every tier of the pagoda, each one a deeper gold than the one above; the topmost lantern swings in a faint updraft, its light sliding across the highest eave.

A stone hill town rides a long ridge in tiers of ochre and bone, houses shouldering upward terrace by terrace to a bell tower whose copper face catches the last alpine light; the switching road climbs from the valley floor in tight ox-blood hairpins, grain-of-wheat bulbs strung along the retaining walls at every bend, and the bell tower's iron door hangs half-open, turning slowly on its hinge.

An English village green spreads under a chalk-white sky laced with drifting pollen, the cricket pitch marked in bone and shadow at its centre, fielders scattered like punctuation across the outfield; the pub beyond the boundary glows amber through mullioned panes, and the church spire behind it rises into acid-green elm canopy above the rooftops; at the crease, a bat leans waiting against the wicket.

An abbey island rises from tidal flats where spray drifts low across the shining sand causeway that joins it to the shore at ebb; buttress walls the colour of old mustard climb above the wrack-line, every lancet window burning deep amber up the nave; the causeway curves slightly left before it reaches the gate, and the gate stands wide, its iron latch swung back against the stone.

A line of windmills strides a frozen polder dyke into a pewter-grey distance, their white sails turning in a stiff cross-wind, each one smaller and hazier than the last; the dyke road runs arrow-straight between them, its cobalt-shadowed ruts glazed hard with ice; squat keeper's houses huddle at the dyke foot, their windows burning burnt-orange behind dark shutters, and snow sweeps low and horizontal across the road, and the nearest mill's brake-rope swings free at the cap.

A dog-sled trail cuts through taiga, the spruce crowding close on both sides in deep bottle-green columns heavy with snow, the packed track curving hard right between the trunks and rising; the team runs mid-curve, a dark low streak of motion, the lead dog already pulling into the bend; ahead through the trees a trapper's cabin burns with butter-yellow light at its single window, woodsmoke rising straight, and the cabin door stands one hand-width open.

A funicular climbs a steep wooded hillside on twin rails of polished cobalt, two vermillion cars passing at the mid-slope loop in opposite directions, their lit interiors burning amber against the dark pines; the upper terminus opens onto a stone terrace strung with butter-yellow lanterns, a café window radiating deep gold, and the lower town falls away in stacked ox-blood rooftops below; at the passing loop, one car's door stands half-open, swinging.

A polar research station squares its huts across a flat white expanse, every structure raised on dark stilts above the ice, each small window a separate square of warm tangerine light; a mustard-yellow snowcat sits parked at the southern edge, its tracks pressed deep; a tall aerial mast at the compound's centre climbs into a sky bruised deep plum and cobalt at the horizon, and one hut door at the far end drifts slowly outward on its hinge.

A great ship rests on the stocks in a deep drydock, its hull a sweep of ox-blood and raw steel, the exposed keel running straight to the far wall; three lattice cranes arc above it, their jibs lit in acid-green flood; a welding arc pulses deep inside an open hull plate, spilling sparks that fall in long copper ribbons through the dry air and spiral along the dock floor, and a rope ladder at the bow sways from the movement.

A river ferry rides a wide jungle waterway the colour of deep moss and umber shadow, its two decks strung with rows of burning lanterns that lay butter-yellow ribbons across the rain-pocked current; the near bank holds a landing stage of low huts, every doorway lit a warm persimmon, a gangplank already run out low over the water; the river bends hard into the tree-wall beyond and carries the lamp-reflections with it, one mooring rope trailing loose and lifting.

A rocket stands on its launch pad under a battery of cobalt-white floodlights, the gantry's folded arms drawn wide to either side, their scaffolding casting long acid-green shadows across the concrete apron; condensation vapour pours from the base vents in rolling white columns and drifts across the pad in slow billows, catching the floodlight and glowing; at the top of the rocket a single amber navigation lamp pulses on its slow interval, still counting.

A red covered bridge spans a dark river in ox-blood timber, its tunnel mouth open at both ends, amber light from the farmhouse beyond throwing a warm corridor through the planks; the river runs fast and copper-coloured beneath, carrying russet and acid-green leaves flat on the current; the lane climbing from the far bank bends into an orchard already deep in shadow, and a loaded cart sits mid-crossing, its wheel caught a half-turn short of the boards' end.

A lone gas station drops to a flat desert crossroads at deep indigo night, one pump standing under a tin canopy whose single bulb throws a hard ox-blood ring of light across cracked asphalt; the road runs dead-straight in both directions and dissolves into absolute darkness at the horizon; dust drifts in slow coils through the lamplight, and behind the station a screen door swings on its spring, batting gently against the frame.

A small ferry holds mid-crossing on a cobalt fjord pressed between two sheer snow walls that drop direct to the water; a mustard-yellow hamlet clusters at the near shore and an ox-blood one mirrors it at the far, every window amber against the blue dusk; the fjord runs deeper between the cliffs and rounds a headland out of sight, and snow sifts straight down through the still air, one flake at a time, onto the flat grey deck.

A reindeer herders' camp spreads among silver birches, its cone tents spaced in a wide arc across deep snow, each one glowing deep plum and amber from the fire burning inside; reindeer move between the pale trunks in loose unhurried groups, their breath steaming; a low sled loaded with rolled hides sits between two tents, and snow falls in large slow flakes through the birch canopy, settling on the folded hide and on the curved tent poles above.

A seaplane sits tied at a lake dock, its floats resting on still pewter-grey water, the fuselage painted deep cobalt with mustard-yellow trim, its wingtip lamp a cold white point; the dock runs back to a lit lodge on the shore, every window burning amber against the dark treeline, and the mountains behind rise in pale blue-violet tiers into cloud; one mooring rope trails slack in the water, drifting with the small current.

A valley of rock chimneys rises in close-packed terracotta columns, every shaft honeycombed with cave houses whose arched doorways burn deep amber against the ash-rose stone; a dove-cote cut into the tallest column shows its grid of niches pale in the last warmth, and a zigzag path connects level to level all the way to a far ridge dissolving into ochre dust; a wooden shutter on a mid-column doorway hangs half-open, drifting outward on the warm updraft.

A blue ice cave opens beneath the glacier in vaulted chambers of deep cobalt and pale aquamarine, every wall transmitting cold Arctic light from above; a climber's lamp burns far inside at the second turning, pooling butter-yellow on the wet floor, and meltwater slides in bright threads down the left wall and disappears into a dark channel below the ice; a rope coiled beside the lamp still turns slowly on its last loop.

A town square opens under a clock tower mid-chime, the tower's face warm ivory above ox-blood brickwork, its hands caught at the quarter-hour, snow settling on the stone ledges in soft even lines; cafes ring the square on three sides, their awnings deep plum and their windows furnace-gold, chairs still occupied by tiny gathered figures; a fountain holds its basin at the centre, the water catching the lamplight in a butter-yellow shimmer, and one cafe door swings slowly inward.

A timber boathouse sits low on a still lake, its dark ox-blood boards reflected in perfect mirror-calm below; a jetty of pale larch planks runs out past the boathouse door and ends in open water where one rowing boat pulls gently at its rope, its oars shipped and dripping; snow comes down in slow vertical lines; a mooring cleat at the jetty's end has a loop of rope still swinging from where the knot was just released.

A whitewashed harbour of cube houses and cobalt domes drops to a small quay in chalk-bright tiers, spray drifting sideways through the water in slow dissolving curtains; ox-blood shutters punctuate the walls at every level, each one throwing a wedge of warm light onto the lane below; a caique rocks at its mooring, its prow rope taut, its sail half-lashed and lifting at one loose corner.

A lava lake seethes in a crater bowl, its surface cracked ox-blood and acid-green where the crust splits and deep furnace-orange bleeds through every fissure; a cinder road spirals up the outer flank in long pale switchbacks, each bend dusted with grey ash that drifts sideways across the road in slow diagonal sheets; a viewing hut on the rim burns with a single amber window, and its door stands half-open against the glow.

A geyser field spreads across a pale silica flat pocked with pools of cobalt and deep plum and acid green, each hollow steaming at its own slow rhythm; the boardwalk crosses from pool to pool on low timber trestles, curving toward the far vent where one geyser has thrown a white column hard into the sky; steam drifts across the flat in long torn scarves, and the nearest pool rocks in slow concentric rings.

An igloo camp sits low on blue-white sea ice, four domes glowing butter-yellow from inside, their round doorways breathing pale light onto the packed snow; a dog team fans out on staked lines to the east, the animals curled tight and frost-furred; a laden sled rests between the dogs and the nearest igloo, its traces still taut, and snow sifts steadily across the ice in thin ground-level streams.

A cathedral square opens wide under a deep cobalt sky, the great west doors thrown back and the nave burning gold inside, light pooling across the stone threshold; market stalls ring the square in a tight horseshoe, their canvas roofs edged with grain-of-wheat bulbs strung pole to pole in warm amber rows; snow falls straight and heavy through the lamplight, and one stall's canvas flap lifts and drops in a slow steady rhythm.

A pleasure pier strides out over pewter-grey sea on rust-lacquered iron legs, its pavilion blazing acid-green and gilt at the far end, spray curling up through the deck planking in long pale threads; the promenade narrows with distance, lanterns halving in size toward the pavilion; a string of pennant lights runs the full length and one pennant at mid-pier swings hard sideways in the unseen wind.

A pastel colonial street of arcaded houses curves gently downhill between facades of coral-pink and mint-green and deep ochre, every arch throwing a violet shadow onto the pavement below; wrought-iron balconies burn with warm amber lantern-light at three levels; a row of bone-white tail-finned cars lines the near kerb, and the street bends out of sight past a bougainvillea-smothered corner; rose petals drift through the warm air in slow spirals, and one balcony door stands open, its curtain lifting.

A stone path to a hillside shrine threads upward through cedar darkness, the trunks iron-grey and close, their crowns lost in layered indigo; paper lanterns in cream and saffron hang at every third bend, pooling gold on the moss-edged steps below; the shrine's copper roof catches the last ember of sky above the treeline; fireflies drift between the cedars in slow green pulses, and the topmost lantern rocks on its cord, still settling.

A stern-wheel paddle steamer rides the wide copper-brown river at dusk, its white decks stacked four levels high and burning with warm citrine light from stem to stern; the great wheel churns a pale wake that fans to both banks and dissolves into slate-blue distance; a landing stage juts from the near shore, its ox-blood timber pilings strung with rope lanterns; sparks gust upward from the twin stacks in bright arcs, and the gangway chain swings loose at the bow.

A stone path threads a bamboo grove in gentle curves, the canes pressing close on both sides in layered acid-green and shadow-grey, their canopy filtering the last amber afternoon light to pale coins on the stone; carved lanterns line the way at measured intervals, each one kindling a soft persimmon glow; at the far end a moss-tiled gate stands half-open onto a courtyard beyond, and loose ochre leaves drift and settle across the threshold.

A chrome diner squats on a desert highway under a sky of deep cobalt bruised plum at the horizon, its long window blazing butter-yellow light across the pale dust of the forecourt; a rust-red articulated truck idles at the near pump, cab lights burning amber; the highway runs dead-straight into black distance in both directions; grit and dust swirl through the air in low slow eddies, and the diner's screen door drifts on its spring, half-open.

A narrowboat sitting low in a canal lock rides the rising water between mossy stone walls, its hull painted ox-blood and cream, the single lock gate half-open and swinging on the slow current; copper-brown leaves drift through the chamber in lazy spirals; the lock-keeper's cottage burns mustard-yellow at every small window, its chimney breathing white, and a coil of rope on the near bollard is still unwinding.

A medina rooftop terrace climbs in broad flat steps above a tangle of ochre and deep-plum alleyways whose lantern glow bleeds upward in warm amber columns; a pale minaret rises at the far quarter, its gallery lit cobalt-cold against the indigo sky; fine dust drifts through the light in slow veils between the levels; a wooden shutter on the highest terrace stands at half-angle, held there by the evening wind.

A row of houseboats moored along a canal bank sits low in still water, their hulls running in stripes of cobalt and burnt-orange and deep plum, every porthole burning warm gold against the grey towpath dusk; snow drifts in soft diagonal lines across the scene; bicycles lean in a line along the bank rail, and at the far mooring the last gangplank rests at a tilt, one end still rocking.

A lavender farm runs its deep violet rows to a stone barn whose broad doors glow with warm ochre lantern-light from inside; the furrows converge on the barn in tight perspective lines, hives set at each row-end wearing their own small caps of white; a farmhouse window burns butter-yellow behind a lace of bare plum-dark branch; pollen drifts in slow gold clouds between the rows, and a wooden barrow rests mid-path, tilted, one handle touching the ground.

A marble quarry drops in wide white terraced benches of pure chalk and cool dove-grey, each level connected by steep ramps dusted bright; a crane stands on the topmost bench, its jib swung out over the drop at mid-arc; fine stone dust drifts through the tiers in slow pale curtains; a cut block rides the flatbed truck on the lowest ramp, the truck's wheels at the edge of the turn, beginning to move.

A wooden stave church rises from a snowy valley on tiered dragon-carved eaves, each roof layer darker than the last against the blue-white ground; a torchlit path cuts straight from the lych-gate across the valley floor and bends at the treeline into shadow; the upper nave window burns deep amber through its leaded panes, and the heavy iron ring on the church door hangs mid-swing.

A stilt village spreads across a dark bayou, its tin-roofed porches strung with amber lanterns that lay ox-blood columns of light down into the black water below; a pirogue poles between the piles along the main channel, pushing a bow-ripple that catches the gold; fireflies drift through the spaces between the houses, and one porch door stands wide with a rocking chair still moving.

A maple sugar bush crowds a low hillside, the pale ash-grey trunks marching upward in close rows, each one hung with a tin bucket at shoulder height; a sled track curves from a gap in the trees down to the sugar shack below, whose open vent breathes a steady plume of white steam into the cold air; snow settles on the bucket lids, and the shack door is propped open with a split log.

A prairie grain elevator stands against a wide oat-coloured sky above a railway siding, its tall mustard-yellow clapboard face lifting to a peaked cap; two ox-blood boxcars sit coupled on the near rail, and the siding track curves away flat into the distance until it vanishes; the lit office window casts a warm square onto the gravel below, and chaff drifts in slow diagonals through the lamplight, and the loading chute hangs angled down, mid-lower.

A canopy walkway strings between rainforest giants at crown height, the rope-and-plank span sagging gently at mid-span above a deep-plum understorey far below; one great trunk at the far end swells into a lodge whose acid-green shutters glow warm gold at every seam, and a second walkway branches left and dissolves into the canopy; rain drifts through the open air between the trees, and a single shutter at the upper level swings on its hinge.

A stone aqueduct carries a canal across a broad valley on tall ox-blood arches, the water dark and glassy between the parapets, amber-lichen streaked down every pier; the valley floor far below is a patchwork of ochre and sage, a river threading it silver; on the high channel a flat-bottomed boat nudges forward mid-crossing, its pole man leaning into the stroke, copper-brown leaves drifting slow across the water around him.

A small country railway station sits at the foot of a pine-dark cutting, the platform edged in chipped white paint, a single lamp burning warm tangerine above the bench; the waiting train stretches five lit carriages along the curve, each window a rectangle of butter-yellow warmth; the signal arm points skyward at the platform end, cleared and eager, and a carriage door stands open at the far end, swinging gently on its hinge.

A hot-spring village fills a steep basalt bowl, stone lanes dropping terrace by terrace toward the steaming pools at the centre; every pool breathes a dense column of pearl-white vapour that climbs and merges above the rooftops; the wooden inns are painted deep plum and warm cedar-brown, their paper-screened windows burning amber in rows; a towel draped over a poolside rail lifts and settles in the rising steam.

A desert oasis crowds its palms tight around a still acid-green pool at the centre of burnt-gold dunes that rise on three sides and roll away to a further ridge; the caravanserai's arched façade glows deep saffron from within, lanterns swinging in each archway, their reflections long on the dark water below; sand drifts in slow amber veils across the pool's surface, and a camel rope swings loose from a hitching post.

A drive-in cinema screen towers bone-white at the far end of a deep cobalt-dark lot, its picture blazing warm rust and gold across the rows of rounded car roofs below; the projector beam cuts a dusty mustard-yellow corridor through the dark from a small booth at the back; moths spiral and tumble through the beam in slow constellations, and one car door at the nearest row stands propped open, a pale arm resting along the sill.

A colliery headframe rises over a slag-black yard, its great iron winding wheel turning slow against a pewter sky, chain-links catching the lamp-room's amber glow in broken arcs; a coal train threads the yard below on rust-red rails, its open wagons heaped and glinting, steam lifting white from the engine stack; the lamp-room window burns deep buttercup behind its wire grille, and a ventilation door at the shaft-head hangs mid-swing on its counterweight.

A mountain pass road runs through snow galleries whose arched stone mouths frame cobalt valley air at three descending distances, the grade dropping hard between each tunnel; a postbus the colour of ox-blood holds the second bend, its lit windows burning warm amber against the gallery shadow, and the road curls beyond the third arch into a far white switchback still catching last light; a single warning post on the outer edge leans at a tilt into the drop.

A bee yard of painted hives spreads across a wildflower field whose acid-green stems and deep plum clover heads press close to the hives on all sides, pollen drifting gold and thick through the warm air between the rows; the hives run ochre, chalk-white, and a weathered cornflower blue, each box distinct; a beekeeper's hut at the field's far edge burns butter-yellow at its one low window, and the hut's screen door rests half-open on its wooden latch.

A river log drive jams a broad muscled bend, the logs locked silver-grey and tight from bank to bank, water boiling dark between them, snow sifting onto the jam and the black current alike; on the near bank a lumber camp of low bunkhouses glows ox-blood at every curtained window, smoke rising from four stovepipe chimneys in straight white columns; a peavey pole leans out over the nearest log, its iron point resting against the wood, abandoned at the balance.

A cattle drive fords a wide tawny river, the herd mid-crossing and the water broken into a thousand dust-pale chevrons around them, red dust still lifting from the near bank and drifting downstream in a long ochre veil; riders hold the flanks on both shores, their horses chest-deep or dry depending on the bank; a chuck wagon stands the far side on high ground, its canvas cover burnt-orange in the late slant light, a cooking fire already going beneath the tailgate.
